items.title: Ladakh bureaucrats worse than Britishers, says activist Wancghuk’s wife Angmo on stalling of kindergarten
points: Gitanjali J Angmo, wife of educator and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk.
File. | Photo Credit: PTI Ladakh activist Sonam Wangchuk’s wife, Gitanjali J.
Angmo, on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) accused the Ladakh bureaucrats of being “worse than Bristishers for stopping a kindergarten school under different pretexts” and termed it “a witch-hunt”.

On the one hand, national institutions ask us to impart lectures on setting up similar educational institutes; on the other, the Desert Flower School, which is a kindergarten level, is stopped from starting admissions,” said Ms. Angmo.

On Tuesday (November 3, 2026), the Ladakh administration said the Himalayan Institute of Alternatives, Ladakh’s (HIAL) Desert Flower School commenced functioning “without necessary approvals from the competent authority”.
She said the construction of the school started in 2023 with the donations of Public Sector Units “after due diligence and compliance”.
Questioning the Ladakh administration’s statement on land lease to the HIAL, Ms. Angmo said the claims made in the government order were “baseless”.

items.title: Spend more time in India: Rijiju takes jibe at Rahul, list conditions for Congress to ‘win more MPs’
points: Taking a jibe at Rahul Gandhi, Union minister Kiren Rijiju on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) listed some conditions for Congress, saying if the Opposition party wants to "win more MPs", then their senior leader must spend more time in India and stop meeting…
Mr. Rijiju has been taking on Mr. Gandhi and other Congress leaders for demanding an open debate with the Prime Minister.
In a post on X on Wednesday (November 4, 2026), he said that Congress can "win more MPs" if Mr. Gandhi meets seven conditions.

Listing these conditions mockingly, Mr. Rijiju said Mr. Gandhi should "spend more time in India and avoid secret foreign vacations frequently." He also asked the Congress leader to respect seniors and gain valuable wisdom from the elders, which is Indian…

"Respect Constitution of India, and honour Constitutional Institutions, and allow Congress party to function as a democratic party and smash dynastic politics," he listed them as the last two conditions.

items.title: Recruitment for more than 11,000 posts in Bihar’s health department to begin soon
points: Bihar’s Health department is all set to begin the process to fill more than 11,000 administrative, technical and medical support positions.

Sharing the information, State Health Society Executive Director Nawal Kishore Chaudhary on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) said the official recruitment notification for this massive hiring drive is expected to be issued by the last week of this month.
Currently, updated details of vacant positions have been sought from all 38 districts of the State.
The information is being gathered from district-level health institutions, Primary Health Centres (PHCs), Community Health Centres (CHCs) and Sub-Divisional Hospitals.

According to the Executive Director, recruitment will be carried out for several positions, including Staff Nurses, Laboratory Technicians, managerial-category posts, Block Health Managers (BHM), NME personnel at the block level, and clerical staff.
Mr. Chaudhary, added that the completion of the first phase of recruitment for more than 11,000 posts will undoubtedly bring significant and positive changes to Bihar’s healthcare sector.

items.title: More than 43 lakh pucca houses completed in Bihar for poor families
points: Under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Gramin) schem, a total of 43,14,959 poor families in the state have so far completed the construction of their pucca houses.

According to figures released by the Rural Development Department, approval for construction of pucca houses for 49,09,740 beneficiaries have been granted against the overall target of 49,16,649 houses set from the financial year 2016-17 onwards.
The Bihar government has spent a total of ₹56,743.40 crore so far on the implementation of this scheme to provide houses equipped with basic amenities.

PMAY-G, which is a Union Ministry of Rural Development’s flagship scheme, aims to provide a pucca house with basic amenities to all houseless households and those living in kutcha or dilapidated houses.
In the first phase, a target was set to construct 37,01,138 houses during the financial years 2016-17 to 2021-22.
A target of constructing 12,15,511 houses has been set under the second phase, covering the financial years 2024-25 and 2025-26.

items.title: Explosion damages railway track in northern Rajasthan district
points: A passenger train had passed through the stretch barely 45 minutes before the incident.
The blast, which occurred near 50 GB village, shattered two concrete railway sleepers beneath the tracks, dislodged the track clips and created a two-foot-deep crater at the site.
The North-Western Railway cancelled four train services on the route on Wednesday as a precautionary measure.
Villagers living about 200 metres away from the spot heard the explosion and informed the police.
While the forensic experts collected samples from the site, the security agencies were examining the vital aspects of intensity of the explosion and nature of the explosive substances used.
Sriganganagar Superintendent of Police Harishankar Yadav said the teams from the National Investigation Agency (NIA) and Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) had arrived to join the probe.
“The district police are carrying out the investigation.
The exact nature of the explosion will be determined after the forensic report is received,” Mr. Yadav said.

items.title: U.P. to match Assembly voter lists with Panchayat and Urban local body rolls to find missing voters
points: The officials said that every effort will be made, with the cooperation of various departments, to enrol eligible citizens, especially youth and women. | Photo Credit: J.

Allen Egenuse Chief Electoral Officer of Uttar Pradesh has directed that voter lists of all Assembly constituencies of the State be matched with Panchayat and Urban Body electoral rolls in order to find eligible citizens missing from the rolls during the…
In an official statement on Wednesday (November 4, 2026), the U.P.

Directions have also been issued to Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) to get Form 6 filled for every identified eligible citizen who is not on the voter list of any Assembly constituency in India.
District Electoral Officers have also been asked to use fair price shops run by the Food and Civil Supplies Department to find those left out.

items.title: Helping hand: On Cyclones Arnab and Murasu
points: Long-term preparedness and a swift response by authorities minimised casualties when the back-to-back cyclones Arnab and Murasu hit two places of the Andhra Pradesh coast.
In Andhra Pradesh, damage from Cyclone Arnab, which made landfall on October 28 was estimated at roughly ₹4,526 crore.
Initial estimates of the damage by Cyclone Murasu, which crossed the coast on November 3, indicate that about 52,500 hectares of standing crops were affected.
The State reported 12 deaths from the two cyclones.
The first cyclone damaged nearly 90,000 hectares of standing crops in southern parts of Odisha.
During Cyclone Hudhud in October 2014, Andhra Pradesh reported 63 deaths and damage estimated at nearly ₹22,000 crore.

The Union government should improve the scheme so that all farmers are encouraged to bring their crops under the scheme, while State governments should raise awareness about the insurance scheme and support agriculturists by topping up benefits that are…

items.title: Alcohol stocks jump as blue wave boosts industry prospects
points: As the midterm elections unfold, investors are directing their focus to the alcohol sector, anticipating positive impacts on companies such as Constellation Brands due to shifting immigration policies.
Optimism surrounding decreasing trade tensions with Canada also seems to uplift brands like Brown-Forman.
However, the looming tariffs have caused a sharp decline in US spirits exports, and overall alcohol consumption in the country is still at historical lows, despite minor upticks.

items.title: Government proposes immediate suspension of manufacturing licences of substandard drugs
points: Representative image. | Photo Credit: Getty Images/iStockphoto The Union Health Ministry has proposed amendments to the Drugs Rules, 1945, to immediately suspend the manufacturing licences of drugs declared Not of Standard Quality (NSQ) on specified…

Under the existing provisions of the Drugs Rules, 1945, suspension or cancellation of a manufacturing licence is preceded by the prescribed regulatory procedure, including issuance of a show-cause notice.
This may result in a time gap between the declaration of a drug as NSQ and the initiation of regulatory action.

The suspension shall continue until the manufacturer undertakes an effective root cause analysis to identify the reasons for the quality failure and implements appropriate Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) to the satisfaction of the licensing authority.
“To further strengthen regulatory coordination and facilitate timely action, consequential amendments have also been proposed to Form 13, relating to the test report of the Government Analyst.

items.title: Musk stocks lose $120 billion as Democrats’ Texas win rattles investors
points: Tesla and SpaceX lost more than $120 billion in combined market value after Democrats scored major election victories in Texas and across the US.
Investors are concerned that a Democrat-controlled Congress could increase scrutiny of Elon Musk’s businesses, complicate a potential Tesla-SpaceX merger and create fresh regulatory hurdles.

items.title: Woman pedestrian killed after being hit by bus in Kochi
points: A 30-year-old woman was killed after being hit by a private bus allegedly travelling at excessive speed at Kuzhikkattumoola near Kakkanad on Wednesday.
The deceased is Akshara S., a resident of Kusumagiri, Kakkanad, and a native of Tholur in Thrissur.
The Infopark police have arrested Binoy, the bus driver, on the charge of culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
The accident took place on Kakkanad-Infopark Road at Kuzhikkattumoola around 8.20 a.m. when Akshara was walking home from a gym.
The bus, which came from the opposite direction, hit her and ran over her.
Though she was rushed to a nearby private hospital, she succumbed to her injuries around 11 a.m., according to the first information report.

items.title: Celebrations among NDA alliance leaders after landslide victory
points: Celebrations broke out among NDA alliance leaders and workers in Vijayawada following the alliance’s emphatic victory in the Vijayawada Municipal Corporation elections.
MP Kesineni Sivanath, East MLA Gadde Ramamohan, NTR district parliamentary constituency in-charge M.
Mallikarjuna Rao, BJP NTR district president Gadde Anuradha and others participated in the programme.
They felicitated the newly-elected Mayor Vangaveeti Radha Krishna on Wednesday.
The MP said the victory had placed greater responsibility on the alliance and assured that they would live up to people’s expectations by developing Vijayawada in all sectors.
The MP said the delay in finalising seat-sharing arrangements within the alliance and certain other factors had cost them victory in another three to four divisions.
He said they were always willing to consider constructive suggestions from anyone, including former IPS officer A.B.
Later, Mr. Radha Krishna expressed his gratitude to Jana Sena Party president and Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan for giving him the opportunity to serve as Mayor and to Chief Minister N.

items.title: Kochi police yet to complete verification of private bus employees
points: The police, according to sources, are planning to issue the ID cards by next week, though they admitted that a final decision on how to proceed with the drive was yet to be taken.
Earlier, the police had planned to complete the process within a few weeks in September and then by the end of October, but the initial plan could not be implemented.
An officer involved in the process said the verification of over 1,500 employees, including drivers and conductors, had been completed.
It is roughly estimated that around 2,000 employees work as bus crew in the city.
Bus employees were asked to submit their personal details to the police in a pro forma for verification.
The police launched the background verification drive in response to a series of incidents involving alleged criminal behaviour by private bus employees in recent times.
The Special Branch of the police is conducting the verification based on the applications received by the traffic wing.

points: Elections for ZPTC and MPTC seats in Velerupadu, Buttaigudem, Jeelugumilli and Polavaram mandals, scheduled on November 5, have been postponed to November 6, due to heavy rains triggered by Cyclone Murasu, said Eluru district Collector K.
She directed the officers to shift the villagers to safer places immediately.
Police evacuated the villagers from Koya Madhavaram, Kummarigudem, Medipally, Allurinagar and other habitations as Peddavaagu is in spate in Velerupadu mandal.

items.title: Direct T.N. DGP to frame guidelines regarding registration of criminal cases for social media posts, political criticism and online speech, insists a PIL plea before Madras High Court
points: The First Division Bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G.
The petitioner had sought a direction to the DGP/HoPF to frame the guidelines on the basis of a representation made by him on August 20, 2026 and circulate them to all the police divisions and wings.

He said, the need for the case had arisen because of increasing number of criminal cases booked against political commentators, activists and social media users for criticism, satire, political opinion and democratic dissent expressed through online platforms.
He said, in several instances, police had entertained the complaints mechanically without examining whether the speech was protected under Article 19(1) of the Constitution.

He said, the Telangana High Court had on September 10, 2025 laid down eight guidelines to be followed by the police to prevent misuse of criminal law in matters concerning political speech and social media posts.
The Telangana High Court had cautioned the police against mechanical registration of criminal cases in matters concerning harsh, offensive, or critical political speeches.

items.title: Two 17-year-old students sexually assaulted at party, two booked under PoCSO
points: Two 17-year-old girl students were allegedly sexually assaulted after being made to consume alcohol at a party in Balanagar on the night of October 1.
Police have registered a case under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act against two youths in connection with the incident.
The suspects have been identified as Ganesh alias Ghana, 19, and Tarun, 26, who is married.
Ganesh was in a relationship with one of the victims and had invited her to the party.
According to Madhura Nagar police Inspector H.
Prabhakar, after taking the two students to the venue, the youths allegedly made them consume alcohol before sexually assaulting them.
“The students had consumed one beer each.
The students were admitted to a hospital in Madhuranagar following the incident.

items.title: Bitcoin rebounds with stocks despite threat to crypto agenda
points: Bitcoin rebounds more than 4% to above $81,000, tracking a broader recovery in financial markets after the US midterm elections.
However, Democratic control of Congress threatens to stall crypto-friendly legislation and increase regulatory scrutiny.
Investors are also weighing the impact of political uncertainty, Treasury yields and institutional adoption.

items.title: Transpacific emerges as liner shipping’s golden trade
points: The transpacific has become the most lucrative major container shipping trade in the world, with carriers generating five times more spot revenue per nautical mile on the Shanghai–Los Angeles route than on shipments to North Europe via the Cape of Good Hope.

At approximately $7,500 per feu, the 5,775 nautical mile Shanghai–Los Angeles voyage generates $1.30 in revenue per container per nautical mile, compared with just 26 cents on Shanghai–Rotterdam via the Cape, or 34 cents via Suez.
Shanghai–New York generates 96 cents per nautical mile, with spot rates remaining above $10,000 per feu since late August.
ZIM, which already deploys 52% of its capacity on the Pacific, will launch another China–California service in December.
COSCO reported third-quarter liner profits of $2.66bn, double the year-earlier level, with transpacific revenue surging 61.2%.
Freightos noted that rates remain approximately $5,500 per feu above pre-peak-season levels, while the approaching Lunar New Year demand cycle could limit the extent of any correction.

items.title: Karnataka will integrate all its skilling efforts into a single unified system: CM
points: Shivakumar interacting with students at the Bengaluru Skill Summit on Wednesday (November 4). | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Chief Minister D.K.

Shivakumar has announced a plan to integrate the State’s fragmented skilling efforts into a single unified system, budgeting an estimated investment of ₹5,000 crore to train 30 lakh beneficiaries over the next seven years.

Speaking at the Bengaluru Skill Summit on Wednesday, the Chief Minister also revealed the formation of a new State Vision Group for skill development, chaired by Mindtree co-founder Subroto Bagchi, to fundamentally reshape the state’s workforce pipeline to…

The policy shift comes at a time when Karnataka, which produces over one lakh engineering graduates every year, has several of them facing underemployment or accepting entry-level positions with low salaries.

With over 550 Global Capability Centres (GCCs) currently operating in Bengaluru and an additional 500 targeted by 2029, the government is rushing to upgrade its vocational training ecosystem before an estimated 3.5 lakh upcoming jobs are introduced to the…

items.title: Visvesvaraya Technological University decides to introduce on-demand examinations for candidates who failed
points: With the introduction of the on-demand examination system, students will no longer have to wait for the university to announce the supplementary examination schedule.
The university will be ready to conduct examinations at a time convenient to students, based on their requests, even for a single student.
Vidyashankar, Vice-Chancellor, VTU, said, “With the intention of providing greater convenience to students, we have decided to introduce on-demand examinations.

Even if a single student wishes to appear for an examination, we will conduct it for them.” VTU has decided to announce the results within 24 hours of the examination for students appearing for these on-demand examinations.
There are 220 engineering colleges under VTU’s jurisdiction, with around three lakh students currently pursuing their studies.
Approximately 70,000 students secure admission every year.
On average, around 20% of students fail in one or more subjects in each semester examination.
There is already a bank of 500-600 question papers for each subject.

items.title: Police Inspector awarded two-month imprisonment in contempt case
points: The Telangana High Court awarded two-month imprisonment to a police officer of the rank of Inspector, holding him guilty in a contempt of court case.
Bhaskar Reddy of the HC also imposed a fine of ₹ 2,000 on Inspector M.
The sentence, however, was suspended for two weeks providing an opportunity to the Inspector for an appeal.
Sekhar Babu and seven others contending that the Inspector failed to provide aid to protect their plots despite specific orders from the HC - passed in 2023.

The petitioners, majority of them senior citizens, stated that despite a specific direction from a single judge of the HC to provide protection to them from illegal interference by three persons (who were made respondents in the writ petition), the then…
The Inspector contended that he had no knowledge of the earlier order of the HC in the matter.
“However, the absence of prior knowledge of the an order cannot justify inaction.

items.title: U.S. Targets Fraudulent Ship Registries Used by Iran’s Shadow Fleet
points: U.S. forces board the sanctioned stateless tanker Majestic X in the Indian Ocean during a maritime interdiction operation on April 23, 2026.
The vessel, formerly known as Phonix, has been linked to Iran’s shadow oil trade.

Photo: Department of War The United States on Wednesday sanctioned a network of individuals and companies accused of operating fraudulent ship registries that helped Iran’s shadow fleet evade sanctions, while issuing a new warning to maritime companies…

The U.S. Treasury Department announced the sanctions on Wednesday as part of Operation Economic Outcast, targeting an India-based network led by Suniel Kumar Sharma and his wife, Jaspreet Preeti Shahid.
Treasury said the scheme dates back to at least 2014, when Sharma and Shahid sought to impersonate the flag administration of Dominica.

In 2023, Sharma established Singapore-based Eswatini Maritime Affairs and International Ship Registry PTE Ltd. , which continued providing registration services for vessels transporting Iranian oil even after authorities in Eswatini publicly disavowed the…

items.title: Police ARSI suspended for allegedly reporting for duty drunk, misbehaving with public
points: The suspended officer has been identified as Gopal B.
According to sources, members of the public objected to his behaviour after noticing that he was allegedly intoxicated.
A heated argument ensued, which escalated when some people allegedly roughed him up before handing him over to Hoysala patrolling police personnel.
The public also demanded that the officer undergo an alcohol breathalyser test to establish whether he was drunk while on duty.

One of the people present recorded the incident on a mobile phone and circulated the video on social media, tagging the Home Minister and the Bengaluru City Police Commissioner and demanding action against the officer.

The video and the incident reportedly caused embarrassment among senior police officials, who directed the jurisdictional Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) to conduct an inquiry and initiate strict action.

items.title: Chief Minister virtually inaugurates Odugathur Fire Station in Vellore
points: The new building was built at a cost of ₹1.35 crore. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Chief Minister C.
Joseph Vijay virtually inaugurated a fire station in Odugathur town at the foothills of Jawadhu Hills on Wednesday.

Officials of the Fire and Rescue Services said that prior to the opening of the building, the fire station was functioning on the premises of the Government Veterinary Clinic in the town for nearly three decades.
Leela Alex inspected the new fire station building in the presence of S.
Baskar, Station Fire Officer, Odugathur, told The Hindu.

Divided into officers’ quarters and the fire station, the new building was built at a cost of ₹1.35 crore on a 2.5-acre plot by the Tamil Nadu Police Housing Corporation Limited with a large training ground for firefighters.
The new facility also has a 40-feet-deep farm well to pump water to these tanks.
The Odugathur fire office caters to at least 60 tribal villages in the region.

items.title: Expert team assesses safety of Sathanur Dam in Tiruvannamalai during monsoon
points: WRD officials said that as per norms under the National Dam Safety Act 2021, an expert team should inspect major dams in the State at least once a decade to assess safety features.
“Such an inspection by technical experts helps make corrections in the structure and operation of the dam as part of enhancing the safety of the facility,” N.
Santhosh, Assistant Engineer, WRD (Sathanur Dam), told The Hindu.
Bajaj, former Chairman, Central Water Commission.
Srinivasan, former Deputy Director General, Geological Survey of India, K.
WRD officials said that among 20 major dams in the State, Sathanur dam is the third largest after Mettur and Bhavani Sagar, in terms of storage capacity and height.
At present, the dam has water storage of 3,769 mcft (51.48%) as against a total storage capacity of 7,321 mcft of water.
While water from the dam’s Left Bank Canal feeds 30 tanks in Tiruvannamalai and 10 in Villupuram, the Right Bank Canal is connected to 48 tanks in Villupuram.

items.title: Damning report: On Justice Muralidhar’s report on Israeli atrocities
points: Briefing the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) last week on the International Commission of Inquiry’s latest report on the situation in Israel and the Palestinian territories, its chairperson, retired Indian judge Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar, did…
It draws on medical records, satellite imagery, forensic analysis, witness testimony and videos posted by Israeli soldiers.

Despite Israeli denials, the report finds that soldiers targeted Palestinian civilians, including infants, by using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to identify and execute their targets with impunity; the report quotes top Israel officials claiming the killings.

Justice Muralidhar said that more than 75,000 Palestinians including 21,500 children and 11,000 women have been killed across Palestinian territories since 2023, and yet “little or no action” is being taken by member-states, including Israel itself.

The Committee had previously called on UN members to halt military transfers to Israel, and pass sanctions against those linked to child abuses, as well as to cooperate with the International Criminal Court to enforce arrest warrants against Israeli…

items.title: Police seize 72 kg of ganja, gutka in Vellore, Tirupattur
points: Searches, using sniffer dogs, were held at public places such as railway station on Wednesday. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement In a special drive, the District Police in Vellore and Tirupattur have seized 72 kilograms of ganja and gukta in various…
The police identified the arrested persons as Rajesh Kumar, 32, Ali Khan, 52, Suresh, 37, Akbar, 53, Harish, 35, and Balaraman, 65.
They belonged to Vellore and Tirupattur.
Based on orders of Superintendent of Police N.U.
Sivaraman and Akshay Anil Wakhare of Vellore and Tirupattur districts respectively, special teams were formed to conduct surprise checks at public places in these districts.
The police said sniffer dogs were also roped in during searches at railway stations, bus termini, and other public places during the day-long drive.
The teams seized 35 kg of ganja and 37 kg of gukta in these two districts.
The police said most of the contraband were sourced from agents in Andhra Pradesh, for sale in industrial regions such as Ranipet, Sriperambadur, Vaniyambadi, Ambur, Vellore and Cheyyar.

items.title: Advanced technology for knee replacement surgery helps faster recovery: experts
points: Sampath felicitating Vernon Lee, Head, Department of Joint Replacement Surgery, Naruvi Hospitals. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement The Chairman of Naruvi Hospitals G.V.
Sampath said on Wednesday that joint replacement surgeries are performed using the American-made CORI robot (CORI Robot - USA) at the hospital as it helps in faster recovery of patients.
Addressing presspersons here, Mr. Sampath said that traditionally, patients undergoing joint replacement surgery will recover in three months.
On the other hand, CORI robot technology used for such surgery at the hospital enables patients to recover in a month.

Mr. Sampath also highlighted that the joint replacement surgery at the hospital is cost-effective with patients from remote areas in Vellore, Dharmapuri, Krishnagiri, Salem, Tiruvannamalai, and from places, including Chittoor, Tirupati, Kadapa, and…
Patients from abroad also visit the hospital for the surgery and return home in good health, he said.

items.title: Who Keeps Crashing China’s Stock Market?
points: China is scrambling to contain a stock-market rout only two years after the previous rescue.
Beijing is dusting off the market-support playbook it deployed in 2024.
The People’s Bank of China is providing low-cost funding for corporate share buybacks and liquidity for institutional investors.
In October, China’s stock market suffered its worst monthly decline in more than a decade.

The blue-chip CSI 300 Index has fallen into a bear market from its late-June peak, while Shanghai’s semiconductor-heavy SSE Science and Technology Innovation Board 50 Index, or Star 50, has plunged as much as 48%.
China Life Insurance Co. , for instance, has scaled up artificial-intelligence-related bets and raised its equity allocation to 19.2% of its portfolio by the end of June, from 16.9% in 2025.

On its latest earnings call, executives at China Pacific Insurance Group Co. acknowledged that equity investing had become “complicated” and that portfolios needed to be managed so market volatility didn’t damage short-term returns.

items.title: MSME training programme held at VIT in Vellore
points: Leela Alex inaugurates the training programme in the presence of G.
Leela Alex inaugurated the training programme in the presence of G.
Viswanathan, founder and president, VIT, Sankar Viswanathan, vice-president, VIT, and Reshma Rajeevan, deputy director, Department of MSME.
In his presidential address, Mr. Viswanathan said that the MSME sector forms the backbone of the Indian economy.
After agriculture, it is the second-largest employer, providing jobs to around 33 crore people in the country.
“Around seven crore MSMEs are registered across the country with Maharashtra leading with one crore MSMEs, followed by Uttar Pradesh with 85 lakh MSMEs.
Tamil Nadu comes third with 62 lakh MSMEs.
Around ₹103 crore worth of scholarships under the scheme have been distributed to students since the scheme was started, in 2008.

items.title: Subroto Bagchi calls for immediate overhaul of India’s vocational ecosystem
points: Speaking at the Bengaluru Skill Summit, Mr. Bagchi, who also co-founded IT firm Mindtree, urged stakeholders to transition from statutory minimum wages to “sustainable wages” for skilled labourers.
Mr. Bagchi pointed to Silicon Valley, where specialised vocations like nurse anaesthetists earn more than computer scientists at the entry level.

He pointed to Japan, where the wage gap between an entry-level worker and a general manager stood at a balanced 1:6 ratio, in contrast with India’s wage differential, which he described as “1 to the power of infinity”.

Bringing mindset under scrutiny, Mr. Bagchi condemned the pervasive middle-class habit of labeling household helps as “servant maids” and lamented the persistent stigma that treats vocational institutions as destinations only for youth who have “gone astray”.
“The policy changes and government funding will ultimately fail unless society fixes how it values the skilled worker,’’ he cautioned.
A major bottleneck identified at the summit was the deep information asymmetry between available elite vocational facilities and the public.

items.title: Bengaluru: Man held for beating employee to death after finding him with his daughter
points: The deceased has been identified as Kiran, a native of Keralam, and the accused has been identified as Anandraj, 45.
Kiran had been working for him for the past few years.
According to the police, Anandraj’s elder daughter is studying in Mysuru and had returned home for the holidays.
He had reportedly noticed that she had developed a close relationship with Kiran.
On Tuesday, Anandraj left home with his wife, telling his daughter that they were travelling to Tamil Nadu and would return at night.
However, the couple returned within a few hours and allegedly found Kiran and the girl together in a room.
Enraged, Anandraj allegedly sent his daughter to a relative’s house in Chickballapur, confined Kiran inside the house and assaulted him with a cricket bat and an iron pipe.
The Yelahanka police registered a murder case and arrested Anandraj.

items.title: Toll plazas on Chennai-Tiruchi national highway gear up for Deepavali rush
points: The State’s first multi-lane free flow, barrier-free toll system at Paranur.
Each time there is a festival and a large number of people travel to their hometowns in the State, the toll plazas on the Chennai-Tiruchi National Highway bear the brunt.
Motorists spend around 20 minutes at all the six plazas put together, waiting to cross the gates.
Nearly 50,000 vehicles travel to Tiruchi on a single day.
Due to the high volume of traffic, the lanes and toll booths are operated 24x7 on all days,” a source in the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) said.
However, those crossing the Paranur plaza, the first one from Chennai, will have a completely new experience this Deepavali.
In the past month, over 83% of vehicles with sufficient balance and clear windshields, have driven through this plaza without any hassle,” another NHAI official said.
In October, a total of 19,18,967 vehicles crossed the plaza.

items.title: CPI(M) and Congress skirmish over 'hasty issuance' of liquor licences in Keralam
points: The Excise department’s “hasty” reclassification of wine and beer parlours as bars, and the almost “instantaneous” approval to open lounge bars at Cochin International Airport Limited (CIAL), had caught the government off guard.

Mr. Satheesan and Mr. Liju accused Excise department officials of jumping the gun and blindsiding the government as it formulated Keralam’s liquor policy for the 2026-27 financial year for promulgation on November 30.

They said Excise department officials had used the LDF government’s controversial decision to empower Deputy Excise Commissioners to grant bar licences as a foil to grant liquor licences behind the UDF government’s back.
The ruling alliance also seemed edgy that the expeditious issuance of bar licences might incense the UDF’s prohibitionist base comprising powerful Christian and Muslim social organisations.
Moreover, the UDF government was also miffed that the issuance of bar licences appeared starkly selective, given that 29 applications were pending disposal in the Excise department.

items.title: Vance Blames His Own Administration’s Iran War for Republican Defeat
points: FILE PHOTO: US Vice President JD Vance speaks during a campaign rally at Tyler Pounds Regional Airport in Tyler, Texas, US, October 13, 2026.

SAUL LOEB/Pool via REUTERS/File Photo Vice President JD Vance on Wednesday blamed Republicans’ midterm election losses on the Trump administration’s eight-month war with Iran, which has driven up global energy prices and left commercial shipping under…
The president himself said so last night,” Vance wrote on X, a day after Democrats won control of both the House and Senate.
The war, launched by the United States and Israel on February 28, has left the Strait of Hormuz at the center of a prolonged military and economic standoff.
The United States has maintained a blockade targeting Iranian maritime commerce, while Iran has continued attacking merchant ships in the Strait of Hormuz and Persian Gulf.
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) issued additional warnings this week, highlighting the continued danger to merchant shipping despite U.S. efforts to secure the waterway.
